topics.title: Coursework & Assessment
topics.summary: UC Davis School of Medicine expects students to independently author all written assignments. Where specific assignments require or permit AI, students must follow faculty instructions.

claims.text: UC Davis School of Medicine expects students to independently author all written assignments.

evidence.quote: Students are expected to independently author all written assignments, demonstrating their own analysis, critical thinking, and reflection.
evidence.title: Acceptable Use of Generative AI in Academic Coursework Policy

topics.title: Exams & In-Person Assessment
topics.summary: In UC Davis School of Medicine examinations, using generative AI tools to research or produce answers for closed-book assessments is prohibited unless faculty or course leadership grants written permission.

claims.text: UC Davis School of Medicine prohibits generative AI tools during closed-book assessments unless written permission is granted.

evidence.quote: Students are prohibited from using GenAI tools to research or generate answers for closed-book assessments unless faculty or course leadership grants written permission.
evidence.title: Acceptable Use of Generative AI in Academic Coursework Policy

topics.title: AI Disclosure & Declarations
topics.summary: Under UC Davis School of Medicine coursework policy, any permitted use of generative AI tools must be transparently disclosed in submissions, detailing the specific tool utilized and the nature of its contribution.
topics.scope: UC Davis School of Medicine coursework AI disclosure standards
topics.evidenceScope: UC Davis School of Medicine coursework AI disclosure standards

claims.text: Any permitted use of GenAI tools must be transparently disclosed, including the type of tool used and the nature of its contribution.

evidence.quote: Any use of GenAI tools must be transparently disclosed, including the type of tool used and the nature of its contribution.
evidence.title: Acceptable Use of Generative AI in Academic Coursework Policy

topics.title: Privacy & Data Protection
topics.summary: UC Davis School of Medicine students are not permitted to use external GenAI tools to generate patient care documentation, except as outlined in UC Davis Health policy.
topics.scope: UC Davis School of Medicine patient documentation and privacy restrictions
topics.evidenceScope: UC Davis School of Medicine patient documentation and privacy restrictions

claims.text: UC Davis School of Medicine students may not use external GenAI tools for patient care documentation except under UC Davis Health policy.

evidence.quote: Students are not permitted to use external GenAI tools to generate patient care documentation, including notes, assessments, or care plans, except as outlined in the UC Davis Heath Generative AI Services and Application Use Policy
evidence.title: Acceptable Use of Generative AI in Academic Coursework Policy

topics.title: Approved AI Tools
topics.summary: UC Davis provides guidance on campus technology access; centralized institutional licensing for students across all commercial LLMs remains an unverified gap.
topics.scope: Campus Aggie AI directory and syllabus specifications
topics.evidenceScope: Campus Aggie AI directory and syllabus specifications

claims.text: UC Davis campus IT provides technology access guidance; enterprise LLM licensing for all students remains an unverified gap.

evidence.quote: In instances where the use of GenAI is permitted, the acceptable use of AI tools in a course is stated in the course syllabus or assignment instructions.
evidence.title: Acceptable Use of Generative AI in Academic Coursework Policy

topics.title: Research & Authorship
topics.summary: UC Davis Library provides evolving citation recommendations for generative AI exchanges; formal campus-wide mandatory publication citation rules remain an unverified gap.
topics.scope: UC Davis Library citation best practices
topics.evidenceScope: UC Davis Library citation best practices

claims.text: UC Davis Library provides evolving citation guidelines for generative AI; mandatory campus publication standards remain an unverified gap.

evidence.quote: Citing your sources helps your readers or viewers distinguish content that is unique to you from information you found elsewhere. Given the rapid development of generative AI tools, guidelines on how to cite generative AI exchanges is evolving.
evidence.title: Citation Best Practices (UC Davis Library)

additionalTopics.title: Academic Integrity
additionalTopics.summary: UC Davis School of Medicine students are responsible for verifying the accuracy and reliability of GenAI content and are accountable for errors or misinformation in their work.
additionalTopics.scope: UC Davis School of Medicine student verification and accuracy accountability
additionalTopics.evidenceScope: UC Davis School of Medicine student verification and accuracy accountability

claims.text: UC Davis School of Medicine students are responsible for verifying GenAI output accuracy and reliability, and are accountable for errors or misinformation in their submissions.

evidence.quote: Students remain responsible for verifying the accuracy and reliability of any information produced by GenAI tools and are accountable for errors or misinformation incorporated into their work.
evidence.title: Acceptable Use of Generative AI in Academic Coursework Policy

additionalTopics.title: Teaching Practice

additionalTopics.evidenceScope: UC Davis School of Medicine faculty instruction and assessment guidelines

claims.text: When assignments grant or require AI use, students must strictly adhere to all instructions provided by faculty.
